input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending picture messages from my phone today. I’ve tried a few times, but they just won’t go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you need anything else from me?

Oh, I really don’t want to change my plan—I’m happy with what I have. If adding more data will help, I’m okay with refueling 2 GB. Will this definitely fix the problem with sending pictures? I just want to make sure before I do anything.
Yes, please go ahead and add the 2 GB for me. I really hope this will let me send pictures again. What do I need to do next?

I just tried to send a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose anything important if we keep trying different things?
Okay, I’m ready, but please go slow and explain things simply. I get confused easily with all these settings. What should I look at first?
At the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or LTE. What does that mean?
Yes, please! I’m not sure how to turn it off. Can you walk me through it step by step? I don’t want to mess anything up.
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see one little bar for signal, it says 2G, and there’s a little phone icon. Is that good? What should I do next?
Yes, I’m ready. Please tell me what to do, but can you explain it simply? I’m not sure what “network mode” means, so I might need extra help.
I followed your steps and now I see four bars for signal, it says 5G, and the little phone icon is still there. Does that mean it worked? Should I try sending a picture message again now?

I just tried to send a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t it working even with the better signal and more data? Is there something else we can try?
Yes, I’m ready to keep going. I just really hope we can get this fixed soon. What do I need to check next?
I checked, and my messaging app already has permission for SMS, storage, and phone. Is there something else that could be stopping my picture messages from going through?
I’m not sure what APN means, but if you think it will help, I’m willing to try. Will resetting this mess up anything else on my phone, like my photos or contacts? I just want to be careful.
Okay, if it won’t mess up my photos or anything important, let’s go ahead and try resetting the APN settings. Please tell me what to do, step by step.
I’ve reset the APN settings like you said. Is there anything else I need to do now, or should I try sending a picture message again? Do I need to restart my phone for this to work?
I’m a little nervous about restarting my phone—will I lose any of my photos or messages if I do this? I just want to make sure everything will be safe before I turn it off and back on.
Okay, I restarted my phone and tried sending a picture message again—it finally worked! Thank you so much for your help and for being patient with me. I really appreciate it!
Thank you! I’m so relieved it’s working now. I’ll let you know if I have any more trouble. Have a wonderful day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

I just tried to send a picture message again, but it still won’t go through. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit worried—will I lose anything important if we keep trying different things?

I understand your concern. Trying different troubleshooting steps will not cause you to lose any important data or messages. These steps are safe and designed to help identify and fix the issue.

To proceed, I will guide you through some checks and actions on your phone to diagnose and resolve the MMS sending problem. Let's start by checking your phone's cellular service status and mobile data settings to ensure everything is properly enabled.

Are you ready for me to guide you through these steps?
Okay, I’m ready, but please go slow and explain things simply. I get confused easily with all these settings. What should I look at first?

Thank you for letting me know. We'll take it step by step.

First, let's check the status bar on your phone. This is the top area of your phone's screen where you usually see icons like signal bars, battery level, and Wi-Fi.

I want you to look at the icons there and tell me if you see any of the following:
- An airplane icon (✈️) which means Airplane Mode is ON.
- Signal bars with numbers like 📶¹, 📶², 📶³, or 📶⁴ indicating signal strength.
- A mobile data icon like "5G", "4G", or "LTE".
- A mobile data status icon like 📱 (Data Enabled) or 📵 (Data Disabled).

Please describe what you see in the status bar. If you prefer, I can guide you to run a check_status_bar diagnostic on your phone if you know how to do that.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
At the top of my phone, I see an airplane icon and the battery is at 80%. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or LTE. What does that mean?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is ON on your phone. When Airplane Mode is ON, it disables all wireless connections including cellular service, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. This is why you don't see any signal bars or mobile data icons.

To fix this, you need to turn Airplane Mode OFF. This will allow your phone to connect to the cellular network and use mobile data, which is necessary for sending picture messages.

If you want, I can guide you on how to turn Airplane Mode OFF on your phone. Would you like me to do that?
Yes, please! I’m not sure how to turn it off. Can you walk me through it step by step? I don’t want to mess anything up.

Certainly! Here's how to turn off Airplane Mode step by step:

1. Unlock your phone and go to the main home screen.
2. Swipe down from the top of the screen to open the Quick Settings menu. This is where you see icons for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Airplane Mode, etc.
3. Look for the airplane icon (✈️) in the Quick Settings menu.
4. If the airplane icon is highlighted or colored, it means Airplane Mode is ON.
5. Tap the airplane icon once to turn Airplane Mode OFF. The icon should no longer be highlighted or colored.
6. After turning it off, wait a few moments for your phone to reconnect to the cellular network. You should start seeing signal bars and mobile data icons appear in the status bar.

Please try these steps and let me know once Airplane Mode is turned off and you see signal bars in the status bar. If you want, I can also guide you through checking the status bar again after this.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see one little bar for signal, it says 2G, and there’s a little phone icon. Is that good? What should I do next?

Thank you for turning off Airplane Mode. Seeing one bar and "2G" means your phone is connected to the cellular network but on a 2G network, which is a very slow network type.

For sending picture messages (MMS), 2G is generally not sufficient. We want to improve your network connection to at least 3G or preferably 4G/5G for better data speed and MMS functionality.

Next, I will guide you to check and change your phone's network mode preference to a faster network type like 4G/5G. This will help improve your mobile data connection.

Are you ready for me to guide you through changing the network mode preference?
Yes, I’m ready. Please tell me what to do, but can you explain it simply? I’m not sure what “network mode” means, so I might need extra help.

Of course! I'll explain simply and guide you step by step.

Your phone connects to the cellular network using different "network modes." These modes are like different speeds or types of connections. 2G is the slowest, and 4G or 5G are much faster and better for things like sending pictures.

We want to change your phone's network mode to prefer 4G or 5G so you get faster data.

Here's what to do next:
I will run a check on your phone to see what network mode it is currently set to. Then, if needed, I will guide you to change it to a better mode.

Please hold on while I check your current network mode preference.

5. Make sure the permissions for "Storage" and "SMS" are allowed or enabled.

I will guide you through checking and resetting your APN settings to the default, which often fixes MMS issues.

Resetting your APN (Access Point Name) settings will not affect your photos, contacts, or any personal data on your phone. APN settings are just technical details that tell your phone how to connect to your carrier's mobile data and MMS services.

Resetting them to default can fix issues with mobile data and sending picture messages without affecting your personal files.

After resetting the APN settings, it is important to restart your phone for the changes to take effect.

Please go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it powers back on, try sending a picture message again.

You don't need to worry about losing your photos, messages, or any other personal data when you restart your phone. Restarting simply turns your phone off and then back on, refreshing its system and applying any changes like the APN reset.
